review.tagline: Desktop and web app to run, fine-tune and export open models
review.summary: Unsloth ships as a desktop app, a web UI (Studio) and a Python library for running and fine-tuning models. It runs GGUF and other open models locally with an OpenAI-compatible API, and trains with LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning and RL methods such as GRPO and DPO. The README claims 2x faster training with up to 70% less VRAM, and exports to GGUF, FP8 and NVFP4.
review.audience: Engineers fine-tuning and locally running open LLMs on their own GPUs
strengths: Fine-tuning covers LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tuning, GRPO, DPO and FP8 pretraining
Claims 2x faster training with up to 70% less VRAM, per README
Exports to GGUF, FP8 and NVFP4 and serves an OpenAI-compatible API
Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, CPU and Vulkan across Windows, macOS and Linux
weaknesses: Scope is broad: desktop app, Studio web UI and Core library each install differently
Server-side tools are on by default; exposing it needs --disable-tools or a strong password
Install relies on curl or irm piped to shell scripts
Speed and VRAM figures are the project's own claims; hardware requirements are not listed
needs: Needs PyTorch, llama.cpp, audio.cpp, Cloudflare (optional remote access)
Models: GGUF, MLX, LoRA, QLoRA, diffusion
